{% extends "docs.html" %} {% from "macros/page.html" import code, page_body, section, toc with context %} {% set page_name = "Slider" %} {% set page_blurb = "Selections from a range of values." %} {% block page %} {% call page_body() %} {% call section("anatomy", "Anatomy", heading=false) %}

Sliders let people pick from a range of values. An <input type="range"> is the control. A wrapping .range (or a <label>) is the host. .slider is the carousel — do not put it on a range. The plugin is Expressive.Range because Slider is already the carousel.

Three variants: standard (active from the start), centered (active grows from the midpoint), and range (two handles, active between them). Horizontal or vertical. Five sizes: XS (the default), S, M, L, XL. Optional inset icon, discrete stops, and a value indicator.

Tokens follow the M3 slider spec (Expressive). The handle is a 4dp stop with a 6dp gap to each track. Active is primary; inactive is secondary-container. The end of an inactive track has a 4dp stop. The value label is a 40dp inverse-surface bubble.

Range is not in AutoInit(). Importing the IIFE bundle calls Expressive.Range.Init(), which starts every input[type=range] already in the document and keeps the active track in sync.

Standard is the default. centered grows the active track from 50%. A range slider is two inputs in one .range host.

{% call code() %}
{% endcall %} {% endcall %} {% call section("sizes", "Sizes") %}

Default is XS (16dp track, 44dp handle). s / small is S, m / medium is M, l / large is L, xl is XL. Scope them on the host.

A leading icon sits in the active track — M, L, and XL are tall enough. stops plus step paints ticks on the active track. Dragging shows the value in a 40dp bubble.

Put the script after the inputs, or call init yourself. There are no options. For a slider added after load:

{% call code() %} document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() { const elems = document.querySelectorAll('input[type=range]'); Expressive.Range.init(elems); }); Expressive.Range.init(document.querySelector('#volume')); {% endcall %} {% endcall %} {% call section("methods", "Methods") %} {% call code() %} const instance = Expressive.Range.getInstance(elem); instance.destroy(); {% endcall %}

Destroy the plugin instance, remove the value label, and tear down its event handlers.
